seeding_notes:
Dense *pseudo-random volumetric seeding* into a large candidate pool, followed
  by an entropy-based ranking and a spatial density rule that keeps at most one
  streamline per coarse domain cell.  This is a practical VTK approximation of

    - "A Streamline Selection Technique Overlaying with Isosurfaces"
      (random seeds in the whole volume -> rank -> select N, density rule that
       keeps only one line per cell), and
    - "View-Dependent Streamlines for 3D Vector Fields"
      (large random pool, per-line linear + angular entropy score with
       alpha = beta = 1, keep roughly the top 30 %, RK4 integration).

  Approximations / omissions (documented deliberately):
    * The view-dependent parts (screen-space occupancy buffer, occlusion-aware
      weighting, semi-transparent isosurfaces) are NOT implemented, because the
      host owns the camera/render window and the user explicitly forbade
      opacity and stream tubes.  The occlusion criterion is replaced by an
      object-space density rule (one line per coarse bin), the standard cheap
      substitute for clutter reduction.
    * "At least one streamline near every critical point" is not enforced;
      instead, seeds are rejected in near-stagnant regions and the entropy
      score naturally favours geometrically rich (swirling) lines.
    * Randomness is produced by a small self-contained deterministic linear
      congruential generator (no external random module), so the result is
      fully reproducible.

seeding_notes:
Record 2 (DIOM, "Difference of Inflow and Outflow based 3D Streamline Placement"):
   seeds are iteratively placed at local maxima of an importance field and the
   neighbourhood of an accepted seed is suppressed so that no two seeds end up close
   together.  A full DIOM matrix (sphere in/out-flux of a dense pre-computed streamline
   set) is too expensive for an interactive host, so this code uses the practical VTK
   approximation: the importance field is the velocity magnitude sampled on the grid
   points, seeds are taken greedily from the strongest samples, and every accepted seed
   suppresses all samples inside a radius (greedy Poisson-disk / local-suppression rule).
   This concentrates seeds on the vent jet and the fast recirculation, i.e. exactly the
   "high flow variation" regions the paper targets.

*  Record 3 (multiresolution streamline seeding plane): a coarse, low-resolution
   rectangular seeding rake is placed across the room to guarantee global coverage
   (context streamlines) in addition to the feature-driven seeds.

*  Record 1 (streamline selection / density control): the total number of streamlines is
   kept small (~45) and short/degenerate lines are discarded so the view stays readable.
